text: US stocks were mixed Wednesday as Nvidia's strong results and forecast failed to hold, with the shares reversing from an early gain to close lower. The S&P 500 slipped 0.2% to 7,323.63, its fifth straight loss and longest losing streak since June, while the Nasdaq rose 0.4% to 24,429.88 and the Dow fell 1.1% to 50,198.17. Hotter rate expectations after Fed minutes, weak health insurer shares and lower oil weighed on the broader market. The TSX closed at 34,578.05, down 2.1%, dragged by energy and gold miners as oil and gold fell sharply. In Europe, indexes dipped and the FTSE 100 lost 1.3% after UK inflation hit a one-year high, while Asia was mixed with Korea's Kospi up about 2%. Closing figures for the STOXX 600 and most Asian indexes were not found.
mood: Cautious and mixed: AI valuation doubts despite Nvidia's beat, rate-hike expectations and falling oil and gold kept global stocks uneasy.

veqt.t: Mixed: S&P 500 -0.2% (fifth straight loss), Nasdaq +0.4%, Dow -1.1%.
Energy and gold miners led a sharp selloff: TSX -2.1% to 34,578.05.
Europe dipped, FTSE 100 -1.3% on hot UK inflation; STOXX 600 close not found.
Kospi rose about 2% on Samsung and SK Hynix after a prior-day low; other Asian closes not found.
